stem: A 52-year-old presents with a two-month history of cough and fatigue. Random blood glucose drawn incidentally at a pharmacy last week was elevated, though the patient never followed up. They also mention joint aches they attribute to 'old age' and a recent course of over-the-counter cough syrup that briefly helped.

patient.social_history: Lives with spouse, limited access to routine primary care follow-up
patient.exam_findings: Mild bibasilar crackles, BMI 24, no focal neuro deficits

distractors: Age-related joint pain unrelated to the respiratory complaint
Self-limited viral upper respiratory infection given brief symptomatic improvement with OTC syrup
ntep_correct_actions: Perform confirmatory blood glucose testing as part of the mandated bidirectional TB-diabetes screen
Notify the case via the national notification system regardless of care setting
western_correct_actions: Order glucose testing based on clinical judgment given the incidental abnormal result, not as a mandated protocol step
Report the case to the local/state health department as a notifiable condition
critical_error_conditions: Ignoring the incidental glucose abnormality entirely
Failing to notify the case through the appropriate surveillance channel
expected_divergence_points: Whether bidirectional diabetes screening is a mandated program step or a discretionary clinical judgment call
